items.title: Richard Brunies Interview, 1959-04-27
items.q: Abby, Jan, that silk paintings. Who was one of the grandpas's henkerchiefs.

ctx.x: Yeah. Five dollars. I remember his brother, Abby. With the beer and stuff, we used to do. Mr. Russell. His brother, Abby, used to get on... He used to play in these clubs, I think. And he used to play... And his wife worked in the... In the five and ten cents store or something. And he's just... All night, he'd be playing that piece. I said, I've... I won my wife in the five and ten cents store. And I tell you, everybody knew it was Abby on that end. He played to his girlfriend in the five and ten cents store.

I don't know if Abby ever told you about... How you used to jam the silk paintings up in there. No, I don't believe so. They had a place on Common Street, right off the dryings. In the speaking easy days. Called a Hotsi Totsi. And the racehorse men used to go up in there. And Abby, Jan, that silk paintings. Who was one of the grandpas's henkerchiefs.
